summary.title: Statistics for Hackers
summary.one_liner: Learn to do statistical analysis with computational methods like sampling, shuffling, cross-validation, and Bayesian approaches instead of heavy theory and jargon.
keywords: how to do statistics with a for-loop
takeaways: Statistical concepts such as p-values and confidence intervals can be approached with computation rather than only with formulas.
Sampling, shuffling, and cross-validation are presented as intuitive alternatives to theory-heavy methods.
Bayesian methods are another computational route to statistical analysis.
A grasp of a few fundamental concepts plus basic coding is claimed to be enough to start doing statistical analysis.
summary.summary: This is the Speaker Deck page for Jake VanderPlas's PyCon 2016 talk "Statistics for Hackers", which was also given in an early version at StitchFix in September 2015. The page text is only the talk abstract, which argues that statistics feels hard because of its jargon of distributions, test statistics, p-values and confidence intervals. The talk proposes replacing some of the theory with computational approaches such as sampling, shuffling, cross-validation and Bayesian methods. The page does not include slides text, so the specific examples and methods are not detailed here; a video link to the PyCon recording is given.
